headline: Skybox and Prologis have filed plans for a $550 million fourth data center building at their Hutto campus near Austin, Texas.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: concrete project news with a useful regulatory backdrop, but regional.
importance_line: Williamson County residents and Texas power customers are affected, and it remains unclear whether the new state freeze and grid-security rules will touch this project.
summary: Hoodline reports, citing Data Center Dynamics, that developers Skybox and Prologis have filed with Texas' licensing department for an 846,300-square-foot, $550 million fourth data center at their Hutto campus, with construction planned from January 2027 to October 2028. The filing follows a 21 Sep order from Governor Greg Abbott to freeze environmental permits for data centers until grid and water audits finish, and a 18 Sep rule requiring large power users to post $50,000 per megawatt before grid studies begin.
notes: Filing date not given in the article.
